drivers.title: Oil jumps on Middle East supply risk
drivers.text: Brent rose about 3% to above $116 a barrel and WTI settled near $103 as fresh Middle East supply worries hit. Oil pressured most of the market and the Dow lost about 650 points.

drivers.title: AI doubts spread past tech
drivers.text: Thursday's selloff started with Meta falling nearly 8% after earnings and a plan to sell new non-voting shares to fund AI spending, which sent buyers into Treasuries. Tech steadied Friday but selling spread to other sectors.

drivers.title: Fed decides Wednesday
drivers.text: Fed Rate Monitor puts about 90% odds on the Fed holding at 3.75–4.00% on 28 Oct after September's hike. The 10-year drifted back to 5.00% Friday after its biggest drop in months on Thursday.

sowhat.text: Strategics and sponsors are still signing and closing deals with the 10-year at 5%: CRH completed its roughly $8.5B Arcosa purchase and EQT agreed to a take-private of QIAGEN alongside ADIA and CPP Investments. Industrial buyers keep adding infrastructure-related capacity, as Trane did with Cancoil.

pitch: Markets were soft on Friday. The S&P slipped about half a percent and the Dow lost over 600 points, mostly because oil jumped again, with Brent above $116 on Middle East supply worries. Second, the AI selloff that started with Meta on Thursday spread beyond tech, which pushed money into Treasuries; the 10-year dipped under 5% before ending the week right at 5%. Third, the Fed meets this week and futures price about a 90% chance it holds at 3.75 to 4%. On the M&A side, deals are still closing despite high rates. CRH completed its $8.5 billion Arcosa deal, EQT agreed to take QIAGEN private for about $12 billion with ADIA and CPP Investments as co-investors, and Trane agreed to buy Cancoil Thermal, terms undisclosed.

quiz.q: Where did the 10-year Treasury close on Friday 23 Oct?
quiz.a: 5.00%, up 4 bp after falling to 4.96% on Thursday.

quiz.q: What odds do futures put on the Fed holding at its 28 Oct meeting?
quiz.a: About 90%, with roughly a 10% chance of another 25 bp hike from the current 3.75–4.00% range.
